another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To help you through this assessment, I need to understand your situation better. 

**First question: How old is your child (or the youngest child if you have multiple)?**

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply. The age categories are:
- **Under 16 years old**
- **16 to 19 years old**
- **20 years old or over**

Please let me know the age of your child(ren).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex is 7 years old. I'm living abroad at the moment and wanted to check if I can still claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that context! So you have one child, Alex, who is 7 years old. That's helpful to know.

Since Alex is under 16, let me navigate to the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check a work-related criterion:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

(Since Alex is only 7 years old, I expect the answer is no to paid work - but I need to confirm this for the assessment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's only 7! He's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's what I expected at his age. So Alex is not in paid work, which means he meets this requirement.

Let me move to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now for the next check:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

(Again, at age 7, this is unlikely, but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a young child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name, so he meets this requirement too.

Let me continue to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check on apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since he's only 7 years old and in primary school, I expect he's not in any apprenticeship. But let me confirm - is Alex in any form of apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not! He's only 7 and in primary school. No apprenticeship.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Alex is not in any apprenticeship, so he meets this requirement as well.

Let me move to the next stage:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now we've reached an important part of the assessment, especially given what you mentioned about living abroad.

**I need to check your residency status.** There are several possible paths that could make you eligible. You mentioned you're living abroad - let me ask some clarifying questions:

1. **What is your residency status?** For example:
   - Do you normally live in the UK (even though you're currently abroad temporarily)?
   - Do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
   - Do you have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
   - Are you a UK Crown servant living abroad?

2. **Which country are you currently living in?**

This will help me determine if you meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm living abroad permanently now - I've moved overseas and I'm not in the UK anymore. I don't have any special status like settled or pre-settled status, and I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that. I've just relocated abroad with my family.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So you've permanently relocated abroad and don't fall into any of the special categories (settled status, pre-settled status, or Crown servant status).

Based on the residency requirements for Child Benefit, the key criterion is that you must **normally live in the UK** to be eligible. Since you've permanently moved abroad and don't meet any of the other qualifying paths (settled status, pre-settled status, Crown servant abroad, etc.), this means you don't meet the UK residency requirement.

Let me navigate to the ineligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me provide you with the final outcome of the assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **Assessment Result: INELIGIBLE**

Unfortunately, you are **not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex based on the official eligibility criteria.

### **Why?**

While Alex meets all the child-related eligibility requirements:
- ✅ He is 7 years old (under 16)
- ✅ He is not working full-time
- ✅ He is not receiving benefits in his own right
- ✅ He is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship

**However**, you do not meet the **residency requirement** for Child Benefit.

### **The Residency Requirement**

Child Benefit requires that you **normally live in the UK** OR have one of the following special circumstances:
- Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Pre-settled status AND actively working, studying, or have sufficient resources (with other conditions)
- Crown servant status living abroad

Since you've permanently relocated abroad and don't have any of these special statuses, you don't meet the residency requirements.

### **What You Can Do**

- If your circumstances change and you return to live in the UK, you could reapply for Child Benefit
- If you have any of the special statuses mentioned above that you didn't initially consider, you may want to contact HMRC to discuss your specific situation
- For more detailed advice, you can visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

I'm sorry you're not eligible at this time. If you have any other questions about this assessment, feel free to ask!
